summary: For the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, We created an interactive visual presentation that tells the untold stories of humanity's abandoned lunar exploration equipment. Over decades of space missions, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments have been left behind on the Moon—not as space debris, but as silent monuments of human achievement. Our presentation acts as a digital scrapbook, highlighting the journeys, discoveries, and final resting places of these iconic machines through engaging visuals and timeline storytelling. This project is important because it makes space history accessible and inspiring, ensuring the legacy of these pioneering machines is remembered as humanity prepares for future crewed missions.
details:
Echoes on the Lunar Surface is an interactive lunar storytelling concept created for the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge. It transforms real NASA Moon artifacts—currently buried in technical archives

How It Works

Interactive Lunar Map: Users click on real lunar landing sites to explore the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), and the Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflectors (LRRR).

First-Person Stories & Quizzes: Each artifact tells its own mission story in simple language, paired with authentic NASA photography and quick science prompts linking Apollo to NASA's Artemis program.

Impact & Creativity

Giving silent space hardware a first-person voice makes complex engineering—like wire-mesh rover wheels and zero-power laser mirrors—easy and fun for young learners and classrooms to understand, preserving lunar heritage.

NASA Data Used

NASA Open Data: LRO QuickMap orbital imagery, NSSDC Master Catalog, and Apollo Lunar Surface Journal.
